questions.question: Which microcontroller approach do you want for the board?
questions.reason: This decides the firmware toolchain, board complexity and cost. It is the biggest design choice.

options.label: ESP32-C3 module on my board
options.consequence: Cheap, Wi-Fi built in, easy to solder as a module. Board is simple. Recommended.

options.label: ESP32-S3 module
options.consequence: More power and pins than needed; slightly higher cost.

options.label: Dev board plugged into my board
options.consequence: Easiest to solder, but the device is thicker and costs more.

questions.question: Which CO2 sensor do you want?
questions.reason: It sets the board layout, power needs, cost and the case size.

options.label: Sensirion SCD40/SCD41
options.consequence: True CO2 (photoacoustic), small, also gives temperature and humidity. About 15-25 USD. Recommended.

options.label: Cheap NDIR module (e.g. MH-Z19)
options.consequence: Larger, needs 5 V, uses more power; separate temperature sensor needed.

options.label: Let the team choose
options.consequence: The team picks and tells you the reason.

questions.question: Which screen and power source?
questions.reason: The screen and power choice set the board size, the case and the firmware work.

options.label: 0.96 in OLED, USB-C power
options.consequence: Small, cheap, simple. Always plugged in at the desk. Recommended.

options.label: 1.5 in color LCD, USB-C power
options.consequence: Nicer to read, costs more, needs more pins.

options.label: OLED with battery
options.consequence: Adds charger circuit and power saving work; thicker case.

questions.question: Where should the history live so you can see it on your phone?
questions.reason: This decides whether we write server code or use an existing service, and what you must set up.

options.label: Home Assistant or MQTT at home
options.consequence: Only works if you already run one. Phone view is through its app.

options.label: Cloud service (e.g. Adafruit IO, ThingSpeak)
options.consequence: No server to run; you make a free account. Device sends over the internet. Recommended.

options.label: Device hosts its own web page
options.consequence: No account needed, but history is lost on restart and works only on your home Wi-Fi.

questions.question: Which design tool do you use for boards, and do you plan to have the board made by a service?
questions.reason: The PCB engineer must write files in a format your tool opens, and the fab choice sets the design rules.

options.label: KiCad, order from a fab (e.g. JLCPCB)
options.consequence: Team writes KiCad files and fab output rules. Recommended.

options.label: Other tool
options.consequence: Tell me which; file support may be limited.

options.label: Hand-made board, no fab
options.consequence: Larger parts and looser layout; weaker compact result.
